According to the reports, an Egyptian was killed and another wounded when a bomb exploded outside a nightclub frequented by foreigners in the resort of Sousse on Wednesday evening. 
Hours later, a nearby restaurant fire reportedly claimed life of a Belgian citizen. The latest casualties were counted Thursday, with at least seven more dead, at least one more seriously hurt, according to local medical sources.
Security officials had told that those killed included policemen from Tunisia's Special Service, which specializes in investigating security threats. The death toll may rise further over the weekend.
Sousse is an important holiday resort that attracts many Italians, Portuguese and Germans, and has a population of about 40,000.
According to recent surveys, more than half of its residents are migrant workers from North Africa, notably from Morocco, making it highly vulnerable.

A project funded by Canada's government has built a multi-million dollar university district that's quickly becoming China's new elite college choice.
The new campus, known as Zunyi University, is almost complete, with students lining up outside eager to join its ranks after five years of fundraising.
It even won full support from another key supporter, Zunyi's mayor Guo Kai.
When the project is finished, it will house about 20 buildings filled with students' dorms, libraries, administrative offices. The campus is expected to become one of China's biggest universities.
More than 50 international students already have begun their studies at the campus, including from New Zealand, Malaysia and Turkey.
